title: Verbascoside targets endothelial HIF-1alpha/ Lysyl oxidase signaling to attenuate glomerular injury in diabetic nephropathy.
authors: Kang, Tianyu; Hou, Bin; Shi, Min; Liu, Huan; Li, Yanan; Li, Kaixin; Li, Shuxin; Wu, Zetong; Xu, Zhaopeng; Li, Mengnan
journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
one_liner_zh: 该文研究糖尿病肾病中内皮HIF-1α/LOX信号及毛蕊花糖苷的抑制作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) drives progressive renal fibrosis and functional decline, ultimately leading to end-stage renal disease. Pathological crosstalk between glomerular endothelial cells and mesangial cells is increasingly recognized as central to DN progression. However, whether endothelial-derived signaling specifically drives mesangial injury under diabetic conditions remains undefined. METHODS: We applied multi-omics profiling to identify pathogenic drivers. Target validation included qPCR and immunofluorescence co-localization in renal tissues. In vitro endothelial-mesangial crosstalk was modeled using conditioned media (CM) from mouse GECs applied to mesangial cells. Verbascoside (VB) was screened via structure-based virtual docking against LOX/LOXL2 and binding affinity (KD) confirmed by biolayer interferometry (BLI). In vivo therapeutic efficacy of VB was assessed in db/db mice. RESULTS: LOX/LOXL2 was robustly upregulated in diabetic endothelia. Inhibiting endothelial-derived LOX/LOXL2 or HIF-1alpha in GECs attenuated HG-induced mesangial dysfunction by reducing proliferation/viability, oxidative stress, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, HIF-1alpha drove LOX/LOXL2 expression. VB was identified as a novel dual LOX/LOXL2 inhibitor. VB-CM mitigated mesangial injury in vitro. VB treatment improved renal function, reduced oxidative damage, and ameliorated fibrosis. CONCLUSION: Endothelial HIF-1alpha/LOX signaling drives mesangial oxidative stress and fibrosis in DN. Verbascoside, a dual LOX/LOXL2 inhibitor, represents a promising therapeutic agent targeting this pathogenic axis.
abstract_zh: 背景：糖尿病肾病（diabetic nephropathy, DN）驱动进行性肾纤维化和功能衰退，最终导致终末期肾病。肾小球内皮细胞与系膜细胞之间的病理性串扰日益被认为是DN进展的核心机制。然而，在内皮来源的信号是否在糖尿病条件下特异性驱动系膜损伤方面，仍缺乏明确结论。方法：我们应用多组学分析以识别致病驱动因子。靶点验证包括肾组织中的qPCR和免疫荧光共定位。体外内皮-系膜串扰通过小鼠肾小球内皮细胞（GECs）的条件培养基（conditioned media, CM）作用于系膜细胞进行建模。毛蕊花糖苷（Verbascoside, VB）通过基于结构的虚拟对接筛选靶向LOX/LOXL2，并通过生物层干涉法（biolayer interferometry, BLI）确认结合亲和力（KD）。VB的体内治疗疗效在db/db小鼠中评估。结果：LOX/LOXL2在糖尿病内皮中显著上调。抑制GECs中内皮来源的LOX/LOXL2或HIF-1alpha可减轻高糖（HG）诱导的系膜功能障碍，通过减少增殖/活力、氧化应激和纤维化实现。机制上，HIF-1alpha驱动LOX/LOXL2表达。VB被鉴定为一种新型双重LOX/LOXL2抑制剂。VB-CM在体外减轻系膜损伤。VB治疗改善肾功能、减少氧化损伤并缓解纤维化。结论：内皮HIF-1alpha/LOX信号在DN中驱动系膜氧化应激和纤维化。毛蕊花糖苷作为一种双重LOX/LOXL2抑制剂，代表了一种靶向该致病轴的潜在治疗药物。
